name: Reverse lunge
summary: Step back and lower until the back knee nearly touches, then drive up through the front heel.
setup: Stand side-on to the phone, working (front) leg nearest. Step the other foot back and lower until the front thigh is level, then push through the front heel to stand.
brief: Stand tall. Step the other foot back and lower until the front thigh is level, then push through the front heel to stand.
why: From the side the front knee angle closes every rep, so reps are counted. The trunk lean is smaller than in a forward lunge and is listed rather than judged.
progression: Dumbbells; deficit from a low step.
contraindications: Kneecap pain on the front leg.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Trunk tipping forward
faults.tip: Lower straight down; the back knee travels to the floor, the chest stays up.

faults.label: Pushing off the back foot
faults.tip: The back foot is a kickstand; the front leg does the work.

faults.label: Front heel lifting
faults.tip: Weight through the front heel is what puts the work in the glute.

faults.label: Folding forward
faults.tip: A little forward lean is fine; folding shifts the load to the lower back.

guide.cannotSee: Which leg is doing the pushing.

points.t: Thigh reaches level; heel stays down.
